definitions.disciplineSpecificSessions: The four schools have different academic calendars, so schedule conflicts are managed by making some class meetings discipline-specific. The schedule lists which disciplines are required to attend each meeting. Even if you are not required to attend a meeting, you may attend if you are available. Recorded or asynchronous sessions may be implemented if necessary. For a Management student, the sessions that are NOT required are 8/28 (LAW intro), 9/4 (ARC/ENV intro), 9/28 (ARC studio travel makeup), 10/23 (ARC and LAW project workshop), and 12/1 (LAW disciplinary workshop).
definitions.workingGroups: Students are divided by lottery into three multi-disciplinary groups, each including Law, Management, Architecture, and Environment students. Each group sets up its own administrative procedures — weekly coordination meetings, file sharing protocols, and working standards — and models a real-world project development team with specific member roles.
definitions.standingMeetingTimes: Each group must establish at least one standing meeting time outside of class when all group members are available to meet together.
definitions.assignments: Detailed assignments, where indicated in the schedule, are described in class and released on Canvas. All assignments are to be done in your project group unless stated otherwise.
definitions.readings: Readings are to be done in advance of the class meeting where they are listed. Each week, faculty highlight which readings are required for the next week and describe optional readings relevant to the next module. All readings are on Canvas, either through electronic reserve or the 'files' section. Questions on reading availability go to the TA.
definitions.finalProject: Each student group produces a comprehensive project proposal including, at minimum: detailed narrative argument supported by data and mapping, legal framework, cost estimate, pro forma and proposed financing, and schematic architectural design and visualizations. More detailed component requirements are posted on Canvas sometime after the first week of classes.
definitions.aiPolicy: AI tools may be used freely provided all use is attributed and documented. You remain fully responsible for accuracy, quality, and integrity of everything you submit, including errors, fabricated citations, or design flaws introduced by an AI tool. Each submission must include a brief statement of which tools you used and how, including tasks delegated and a representative sample of prompts. Fuller documentation must be provided on request. Undisclosed or undocumented use is treated as an academic integrity violation and referred to the Rules Committee.
definitions.clinicalExpectations: Clinical work requires the highest level of professionalism. Punctual attendance is expected at all classes, supervision sessions, and client meetings. All client work is strictly confidential at the discretion of the project partner. Personal experiences shared in class or supervision remain confidential. No recording of classes, supervision, or client meetings without permission. Students are expected to check email at least four times per day and respond to client emails typically within twenty-four hours.
definitions.stylesheet: Writing and citations shall conform to the Chicago Manual of Style, 17th Edition (2017).

gradingPolicy: The syllabus does not state a numeric grading breakdown. Evaluation is described qualitatively through the clinical expectations and the Clinic's Evaluation Criteria: professionalism, punctual attendance at all classes, supervision sessions and client meetings, active participation in discussions and presentations, and engagement with the group project proposal. Confirm the grading basis with the coordinating faculty.
